title: She Was Named Sita and Raised to Kill: Alpha Is About to Blow the Spy Universe Wide Open
excerpt: Alia Bhatt and Sharvari lead Bollywood's first female-driven spy blockbuster as deadly assassins, Bobby Deol plays the villain who created them, Hrithik Roshan's cameo seals the franchise connection — and the trailer's 75-million-view first day says the hype is very, very real.
body:
The trailer opens on a glass enclosure. An infant is inside. **Bobby Deol** looks down at her, names her Sita — after her mother, Janaki — and from that moment, nothing about this film is gentle.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=QRqGwGwo1Y0</youtube>

Welcome to **Alpha**, the seventh entry in Yash Raj Films' blockbuster Spy Universe, and the one that might just rewrite everything about it. Directed by **Shiv Rawail** in his feature-film debut, the film stars **Alia Bhatt** and **Sharvari** as deadly operatives in what the studio calls "the origin story of India's most dangerous women." It hits theatres on July 3 — and based on what the trailer delivered, it's shaping up to be the biggest event film of the Indian summer.

Let's talk about what that trailer did. When the teaser dropped on June 10, it clocked 75 million views across platforms in the first 24 hours. Within minutes, **SS Rajamouli**, **Shah Rukh Khan**, **Priyanka Chopra**, **Salman Khan**, **Katrina Kaif**, **Jr NTR**, and **Vicky Kaushal** had publicly praised it. By the time the full trailer arrived on June 17, the conversation had only grown louder — and the green-eyed cameo in the final frame made sure it stayed that way.

Alia shows up looking like nobody's version of the girl next door. The trailer paints her character, Sita, as something closer to a weapon than a person — raised from childhood by Bobby Deol's Fateh Singh Lakhawat, trained in combat, sculpted into a killing machine. This isn't a conventional spy thriller. This is a revenge origin story, brutal and intimate, with Alia doing things on screen — hand-to-hand combat, tactical operations, gunfights filmed across Mumbai, Kashmir, and Valladolid in Spain — that she has never attempted before.

> "I had such a good time making Alpha" — Alia Bhatt

Bobby Deol, meanwhile, is having the career renaissance that keeps getting more interesting. After *Animal*, after *Kanguva*, after being reborn as Bollywood's favourite villain, he now plays a rogue operative running a covert program called Alpha — one that produces child soldiers and weaponises them against India. His dynamic with Alia's Sita is the spine of the film: he names her, raises her, trains her, and she discovers he's been the enemy all along. It's the kind of father-daughter betrayal arc that could power a franchise by itself.

Then there's **Sharvari**. The trailer deliberately keeps her character under wraps — we see her make a colourful, high-energy entrance, trade blows with Sita in a fight sequence, and then, in a twist, join forces with her against Bobby Deol. The studio has confirmed that her arc contains a reveal so significant they're holding it back from all marketing material. Between this and her scene-stealing year — from *Maharaj* to dominating India's Got Latent alongside Alia during the Alpha press tour — Sharvari is building a filmography that dares you to look away.

**Anil Kapoor** completes the lead cast as Colonel Vikrant Kaul, the R&AW chief who mentors Sita once she breaks free. And then comes the moment that broke the internet. In the trailer's closing seconds, a figure in white sits in a monastery, and the camera finds a pair of unmistakable green eyes. **Hrithik Roshan**, reprising his role as Major Kabir Dhaliwal from *War*, seals Alpha's place in the Spy Universe timeline — and confirms that this franchise has plans that stretch well beyond one film.

The production pedigree is formidable. Written by **Soumil Shukla**, **Shridhar Raghavan**, and **Ishita Moitra**, from a story by **Uday Chopra**, Alpha was shot by cinematographer Rubais in a cold, desaturated palette that sets it apart from the glossier entries in the franchise. This is a spy film that looks like it was directed by someone who grew up watching *Sicario* and *Hanna*, not *Dhoom*.

For the diaspora, the timing couldn't be better. With the July 4 long weekend in the United States falling a day after release, Alpha is positioned perfectly for opening-weekend plans. Expect wide releases across North America, the UK, and the Gulf — YRF's international distribution machine rarely misses, and with the Spy Universe brand carrying over ₹3,000 crore in collective worldwide gross across *Ek Tha Tiger*, *War*, *Pathaan*, and the rest, screen counts should be massive.

Six days. Alia has a knife and a name she didn't choose. Bobby Deol has a plan that's about to unravel. And somewhere in a monastery, Hrithik is watching with those green eyes.

The Alpha girls are here.
